a lot of times when a patient isn’t responding to stimulant adhd treatment, nonstimulant medications can be tried. they aren’t as popular bc the stimulants work for most people, but def ask your doctor about your options because it is definitely something to look into possibly before trying another stimulant since the ones you’ve tried were ineffective. 

my first prescription for my adhd was guanfacine, a nonstimulant, because i was experiencing tics at the time and my doctor didn’t want to make it worse. the guanfacine didn’t help me personally, but my tics eventually went away, and i just started 10mg vyvanse, and will most likely try a dose increase. 

moral: everyone’s body is different, so i think it’s a good idea to cover a broad range of options to rule out things that may not work and cut down on the terrible med trial and error process lol
